checks.evidence: Sheffield says hsCRP should not be a substitute for assessment of traditional cardiovascular risk factors.
Sheffield advises people with active infection, inflammation or trauma wait until settled before hsCRP-based CVD risk assessment.
Returned text said current UK CVD risk guidelines do not recommend hs-CRP testing; 'recent studies suggest it may help identify risk in healthy people' not seen.
checks.newSentence: Lab Tests Online UK says current UK guidelines on cardiovascular risk assessment do not recommend hs-CRP testing.

checks.evidence: StatPearls: mild CRP elevations may occur in the absence of overt systemic inflammation.
Scottish guideline PDF not returned; other sources only generally say CRP alone cannot reliably separate bacterial from viral infection, not attributable to that URL.
NHS Highland GCA page: rarely see GCA with normal inflammatory markers; CRP, PV or both should be raised.
checks.newSentence: A Scottish NHS guideline on giant cell arteritis says it is rare to see the condition with normal inflammatory markers, and that CRP, plasma viscosity or both should be raised.
